Requests
Requests is a Python library (version 2.32.3) used for making HTTP requests.

Python-Dotenv
Python-Dotenv is a Python library (version 1.0.1) used for loading environment variables from a .env file.

Life Audit
A self-assessment practice where key life areas such as health, relationships, career, finances, mental health, and fun are rated 1–10 and analyzed for patterns, self-deception, and highest-leverage changes.<SEP>A life audit is a self-reflection exercise where key life domains such as health, relationships, career, and finances are rated and described honestly to identify patterns and high-leverage changes.<SEP>A life audit is a self-assessment method where key life areas such as health, relationships, career, and finances are rated 1–10 to identify patterns and high-leverage changes.<SEP>A structured self-assessment method where key life areas such as health, relationships, career, and finances are rated and described honestly to identify patterns and high-leverage changes.

Hard Conversation Rehearsal
A practice of writing out a difficult situation, feelings, and fears, then using AI to clarify goals, craft constructive wording, and roleplay the other person's likely response.<SEP>Hard conversation rehearsal is an AI-assisted method to clarify one's real needs, phrase messages honestly without being destructive, and roleplay likely responses before engaging in a difficult conversation.

AI
An accessible conversational tool used as a nightly or morning instrument to facilitate structured self-reflection, pattern recognition, and personal development across multiple life domains.<SEP>Artificial Intelligence used as a nonjudgmental external thinking partner to support self-awareness, personal growth, reflection, and structured self-conversation.

Self-Sabotage Analysis
A reflective method where five moments of quitting, avoiding, failing, or getting stuck are described and analyzed to identify an underlying core fear, limiting belief, and hidden payoff.

Personal Operating System
A personalized set of 5–7 guiding principles distilled from an individual's regrets, proudest moments, hard lessons, and values, formatted as a daily personal code.<SEP>A personal operating system is a set of 5–7 core guiding principles distilled from regrets, proud moments, hard lessons, and non-negotiable values, used as a daily decision-making code.<SEP>A personal operating system is a customized set of 5–7 guiding principles derived from an individual's regrets, proud moments, and values, used as a daily decision-making code.<SEP>A set of 5–7 personalized guiding principles distilled from an individual's biggest regrets, proudest moments, and hard-earned lessons, intended to serve as a personal decision-making code.

Emotional Trigger Decoding
A real-time emotional processing practice where one describes what happened, names emotions, rates intensity, and uses AI-guided questioning to trace reactions to deeper roots such as past patterns, unmet needs, and original wounds.<SEP>Emotional trigger decoding is a step-by-step AI-assisted process to trace intense emotional reactions to their deeper sources, such as unmet needs or earlier experiences, framed as therapy-adjacent reflection.

Accountability System
A motivation-independent system using tiny-habit design to create small, failproof starts, with AI checking in, tracking streaks, adjusting the system, and restarting without shame after lapses.<SEP>An accountability system is a motivation-independent structure built on tiny habits designed to be "so small you can't fail," with consistent check-ins, streak tracking, and shame-free restarts.<SEP>An accountability system is a motivation-proof structure designed to maintain habits through small achievable starts, check-ins, streak tracking, and shame-free restarts.<SEP>A structured system designed to track habits and streaks, check in with specific questions, adjust the system rather than the goal, and allow shame-free resets after lapses.

Letter Writing Exercise
An expressive writing technique used to process unresolved relationships or unfinished emotional business, with AI reflecting back core emotions and unmet needs to help craft a final version for personal closure.

BJ Fogg
BJ Fogg is referenced as the creator of tiny-habit design, a behavioral methodology that makes habit starts so small they are nearly impossible to fail.<SEP>BJ Fogg is referenced as the originator of the "so small you can't fail" habit-building approach, cited in the context of designing effective accountability systems.<SEP>BJ Fogg is referenced in the context of tiny habits, a behavioral design approach where habits are made so small they cannot fail.<SEP>A researcher associated with the "tiny habits" approach, which involves designing habits so small that failure is nearly impossible, referenced in the context of motivation-proof accountability systems.

Tiny-Habit Design
A behavioral design framework attributed to BJ Fogg that makes the start of a habit so small it cannot be failed, used as a foundation for building reliable accountability systems.

Prompt Framework
A structured set of instructions or templates used to guide AI interactions for specific self-reflection and personal development purposes.

Structured Self-Conversation
A practice of spending intentional time, as little as 10 minutes, in reflective dialogue to regain clarity, spot patterns, and build momentum in life, facilitated by AI.

Mindless Consumption
The practice of scrolling others' opinions without intentional engagement, contrasted with structured self-reflection as a less productive use of time and attention.

Expressive Writing
Expressive writing is an uncensored writing exercise directed at someone or oneself to unload unresolved feelings, aided by AI to identify core emotions and craft a final honest letter for closure.<SEP>A writing technique used to process unresolved emotional experiences and relationships, forming the basis of the Letter Writing Exercise.<SEP>A technique involving writing to unload unresolved emotions, used in the "letter you'll never send" exercise to achieve emotional closure by reflecting core emotions and unmet needs.<SEP>Expressive writing is the practice of writing unfiltered, uncensored thoughts and emotions as a way to process and release unresolved feelings.

Dopamine
Dopamine is described as a neurochemical associated with anticipation rather than reward, used to explain why motivation is considered unreliable as a basis for habit formation.<SEP>Dopamine is described as the neurochemical driving motivation through anticipation, which fades after planning, explaining why willpower alone is insufficient for habit maintenance.<SEP>A neurotransmitter tied to anticipation rather than sustained motivation, cited as the reason motivation is unreliable and accountability systems are needed.

Original Wound
A foundational emotional injury from the past that underlies present-day emotional triggers and reactions, identified through the Emotional Trigger Decoding method.<SEP>The original wound refers to the deeper emotional source or earlier experience to which intense emotional reactions can be traced during emotional trigger decoding.

Core Fear
A deep-seated fear identified through Self-Sabotage Analysis as an underlying driver of self-defeating behaviors.

Claude
Claude is an AI tool mentioned alongside ChatGPT as an example of AI systems that can serve as nonjudgmental external thinking partners for personal growth.<SEP>Claude is an AI assistant/model used for building AI apps, capable of reading/writing files, running shell commands, and connecting to external systems via APIs and MCP.<SEP>Claude is an AI model developed by Anthropic, available in variants including Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus, used for tasks ranging from simple queries to complex reasoning.<SEP>Claude is an AI assistant (also referred to as Claude Code) that can perform tasks such as reading/writing files, running shell commands, and generating responses based on prompts.<SEP>Claude is an AI system (Claude Code) that can access files, create/edit files, run shell commands, and perform complex AI-assisted tasks for users.<SEP>Claude is an AI system developed for coding and general assistance, capable of searching data, answering questions, editing files, running shell commands, and cooperating with sub-agents.

Introspection Illusion
The introspection illusion is a cognitive bias where people believe they are self-aware but often cannot accurately perceive their own patterns and blind spots.<SEP>The introspection illusion is the concept that the human mind struggles to evaluate itself accurately, leading to biased self-reflection.<SEP>A cognitive bias where humans, when looking inward, tend to protect their self-image and rationalize rather than perceiving themselves clearly.

Self-Awareness
Self-awareness is described as the biggest predictor of success across relationships, career, health, and well-being, with research suggesting only 10–15% of people are truly self-aware.<SEP>Self-awareness is described as the most powerful use of AI, contrasted with productivity, and noted as rare among people due to biased self-perception.<SEP>A skill strongly linked to success and well-being; research suggests only 10–15% of people are genuinely self-aware, often hindered by the introspection illusion.

Hidden Payoff
The hidden payoff is the psychological protection provided by self-sabotaging patterns, often shielding individuals from judgment or evaluation.<SEP>The hidden payoff is the unconscious benefit or protection that a self-sabotage pattern provides to an individual, shielding them from deeper fears or discomfort.<SEP>The underlying benefit or protection that a self-sabotage pattern provides to an individual, shielding them from a perceived deeper fear or threat.

Self-Sabotage
Self-sabotage refers to recurring behaviors such as quitting, avoiding, or getting stuck, analyzed as symptoms of deeper core fears, limiting beliefs, and hidden payoffs.

Cognitive Dissonance
Cognitive dissonance is the tendency to avoid discomfort, which leads people to shy away from honest self-reflection.

ChatGPT
ChatGPT is an AI tool described as an "externalized thinking partner" that helps users gain self-awareness, identify patterns, and reflect more honestly on their lives.<SEP>ChatGPT is an AI tool discussed in the video as a powerful means for self-awareness, personal growth, and structured self-reflection rather than just productivity.<SEP>An AI tool referenced as an example of AI technology that can be used for self-awareness and personal development rather than just productivity tasks.

Psychological Distance
Psychological distance is the mental clarity and emotional regulation gained by externalizing and writing down thoughts, which helps individuals evaluate their situations more objectively.<SEP>Psychological distance is the mental separation AI creates between a person and their thoughts, helping them observe patterns and blind spots more objectively.<SEP>A cognitive state created by externalizing thoughts into structured dialogue, which improves clarity and emotional regulation by separating the individual from their immediate emotional experience.

Limiting Belief
A restrictive belief identified through Self-Sabotage Analysis that contributes to patterns of self-sabotage and avoidance.

Human Relationships
Personal connections between people that AI is explicitly noted should not replace, though AI can support and improve real-life conversations and decisions.<SEP>Human relationships are real-world interpersonal connections that AI is explicitly noted as unable to replace, but can help individuals show up better within.

Self-Sabotage Pattern
Self-sabotage patterns are recurring behaviors such as quitting, avoiding, or procrastinating, which share an underlying fear, belief, or hidden payoff that protects the individual from something.

Therapy
Therapy is a professional mental health practice that AI tools like ChatGPT are explicitly noted not to replace, despite their utility in self-reflection.<SEP>Professional mental health support that AI is explicitly noted should not replace, though AI can meaningfully support reflection alongside it.<SEP>Therapy is professional mental health support, explicitly noted in the video as something AI cannot and should not replace, though AI can serve as a therapy-adjacent reflection tool.

Unsent Letter
An unsent letter is an unfiltered expressive writing exercise addressed to another person or one's past self, used to release unresolved emotions and identify unmet needs.<SEP>A writing exercise in which unspoken anger, grief, or love toward someone or one's past self is expressed, with AI helping reflect unmet needs and produce a final unfiltered version aimed at emotional closure.

Emotional Trigger
An emotional trigger is a disproportionate emotional reaction to a surface event that points to a deeper underlying wound or unmet need.

Tiny Habits
Tiny habits is a behavioral approach associated with BJ Fogg, where habit starts are made extremely small to ensure consistent success without reliance on motivation.<SEP>A habit-formation approach, associated with BJ Fogg, that involves creating starter habits so small they cannot be failed, used to build accountability systems that do not rely on motivation.

Difficult Conversation Rehearsal
Difficult conversation rehearsal is a practice method where an individual clarifies their needs, crafts honest language, and roleplays the other person's likely responses before having a real conversation.

TikTok Video Script
A video script format summarizing seven practical ways to use AI for personal growth, emphasizing self-awareness and structured self-conversation over productivity tasks.

Pattern Recognition
A capability of AI that makes it especially useful for identifying recurring behaviors, self-deception, and emotional patterns across multiple data points shared by the user.

Human Connection
Human connection is emphasized as something that AI tools like ChatGPT should not replace, even while being used to deepen self-reflection.

Difficult Conversations
A practical technique involving clarifying what one needs from a conversation, crafting honest-but-non-destructive wording, and roleplaying the other person's likely responses to prepare for challenging interpersonal exchanges.

YouTube Shorts Script
A video script format summarizing how AI can function as an externalized thinking partner for self-awareness, covering seven practical uses with prompt frameworks.

Emotional Triggers
Reactions involving being overreactive or emotionally flooded, which can be traced through step-by-step questioning to deeper sources, old wounds, or recurring patterns.

Self-Sabotage Patterns
Recurring behaviors such as quitting, avoiding, or getting stuck, which are analyzed to uncover deeper fears, core beliefs, and hidden payoffs that protect the individual from perceived threats.

Checkpoints And Undo
Checkpoints and Undo is a Claude feature that auto-saves project states and allows users to revert edits, providing safety when Claude modifies files.<SEP>Checkpoints and undo is a feature in Claude that auto-saves changes and allows users to revert to previous versions.<SEP>A feature in Claude Code that automatically saves progress and allows users to revert changes, providing a safety net during development.

Claude Code
Claude Code is an AI-powered coding tool developed by Anthropic, featuring concepts such as tools, permission modes, context windows, and sub-agents for software development tasks.<SEP>Claude Code is a tool or framework built around Claude that enables developers and non-technical users to build, connect systems, and use power features like sub-agents and checkpoints.

Sub-Agents
Sub-agents are specialized AI helpers that cooperate on different tasks, functioning like multiple agents in an AI "agency."<SEP>Sub-agents are multiple specialized AI agents that work together, like an AI agency, to split and handle complex tasks collaboratively.<SEP>Sub-agents are multiple specialized AI helpers that coordinate to divide and handle complex workflows, functioning like an AI agency.<SEP>Sub-agents are multiple specialized AI helpers that cooperate within an AI agency framework to complete complex tasks.

Claude.md
Claude.md is a project-specific long-term memory file (MD format) created using the /init command to store persistent project information and avoid repeating context.<SEP>Claude.md is a file created with the /init command that stores long-term project memory and persistent context for Claude Code projects.<SEP>Claude.md is a markdown file created via /init that serves as a project's long-term memory, preserving context across sessions.<SEP>Claude.md is a project long-term memory file created via the /init command, recommended for every repository to maintain persistent project context.

Bypass Permission
Bypass permission is a command that allows Claude to skip repeated permission prompts and automatically make edits, recommended only when the user trusts Claude and has backups.<SEP>Bypass permission (dangerous_skip_permission) is a mode that speeds up workflows by skipping permission prompts, but requires caution and is recommended only when backups or undo are available.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
RAG is a method where Claude searches user-provided data and answers based on that source, enabling more accurate and contextually grounded responses.

Sonnet
Sonnet is a Claude model variant offering a balanced performance and cost-effectiveness, recommended for drafting work.<SEP>Sonnet is a balanced and cost-effective Claude model variant suitable for general and deeper work, recommended for drafting.<SEP>Sonnet is a Claude model variant that balances speed and capability, recommended for many general uses including drafting and organizing work.<SEP>Sonnet is a Claude model variant that is balanced and recommended for general use, including drafting and organizing work.<SEP>Sonnet is a Claude model variant that is balanced and cost-effective, recommended for general work.

Opus
Opus is the most capable Claude model variant, best suited for complex reasoning and multi-step tasks, but more expensive.<SEP>Opus is the most capable Claude model variant, offering the best reasoning for complex and multi-step tasks, though it is costlier, recommended for verification.<SEP>Opus is a Claude model variant offering the best reasoning and multi-step task performance, though it is costlier than other variants.<SEP>Opus is a Claude model variant with the best reasoning capability, suited for multi-step planning and verifying complex work, but more expensive.<SEP>Opus is a Claude model variant with the best reasoning capability but is more expensive, recommended for complex reasoning tasks.

Haiku
Haiku is a Claude model variant optimized for speed and low cost, suitable for fast, lightweight tasks.<SEP>Haiku is a Claude model variant designed for fast, cheap, and simple tasks.<SEP>Haiku is a Claude model variant that is the fastest and cheapest, best suited for simple tasks.<SEP>Haiku is a Claude model variant that is fast and cheap, suited for simple tasks.<SEP>Haiku is a Claude model variant that is fast and cheap, recommended for quick tasks.

Model Context Protocol (MCP)
MCP is a protocol that acts like a master key, allowing Claude broader control over applications on the user's behalf, going beyond standard API access.

API
An API (Application Programming Interface) is a key that allows apps to communicate with each other, providing limited and controlled access.<SEP>An API (Application Programming Interface) is a key that grants limited, controlled access to an application or service.<SEP>An API (Application Programming Interface) is a key or interface that allows external applications and services to communicate with each other, such as the Notion API.<SEP>An API is a key used to access specific functionality of an application, likened to a door key.<SEP>An API is a key used to access specific application features, described as providing limited access points to app functionality.

Context Window
The context window is Claude's short-term chat memory with an input/output token limit; it can fill up during long conversations, supporting up to approximately 1 million tokens.<SEP>The context window refers to the short-term chat history available to Claude during a session, with a capacity cited as up to 1 million tokens.<SEP>The context window is the model's short-term memory, consisting of chat history, and has a finite size limit.<SEP>The context window is Claude's short-term memory for the current chat session, with an input/output token limit.<SEP>The context window is Claude's short-term memory for a chat session, which has a size limit and can be managed by compacting conversation history.

Tokens
Tokens are the measurement unit for Claude's usage and cost, roughly corresponding to units of text or words processed.<SEP>Tokens are the unit of usage and cost for Claude, roughly equivalent to one word each; Claude charges by tokens, making usage monitoring important.<SEP>Tokens are the unit of text processing in Claude, roughly equivalent to one word each, and their usage incurs costs that scale with plan size.

Plan Mode
Plan mode is a safe permissions mode in which Claude proposes changes before executing them, recommended for learning or working on live projects.<SEP>Plan mode is a permission mode in Claude Code recommended for safety, where Claude plans actions before executing them.<SEP>Plan mode is a permissions mode in Claude that is considered the safest option for working on live or sensitive projects, requiring approval before making changes.<SEP>Plan mode is a permission mode in Claude that generates a plan without changing code, recommended for live or important projects.<SEP>Plan mode is a safe permission setting in Claude where no edits are made, allowing users to review planned actions before execution.

Terminal / CLI
The terminal or CLI (Command-Line Interface) is a text-based interface for controlling a computer and running commands.<SEP>The Terminal/CLI (Command-Line Interface) is a text-based interface used to give commands to a computer, such as opening folders or running installations.<SEP>The terminal or command-line interface (CLI) is a text-based tool for instructing a computer to perform tasks instead of using a graphical interface.<SEP>The Terminal or CLI (Command Line Interface) is a text-based interface used to give commands to a computer, relevant to running Claude Code.

JSON
JSON is a structured data format used by computers to organize information, which Claude can generate and format on behalf of users.<SEP>JSON is a structured data format used by computers to organize and exchange information, which Claude can generate and organize.<SEP>JSON is a structured data format used for organizing information, preferred by computers for data exchange.<SEP>JSON is a structured data format used to organize information, preferred by computers for data exchange.<SEP>JSON is a structured data format used by computers, referenced in the context of data exchange with Claude and connected systems.

Git
Git is a version control system that tracks changes in code files, allowing users to revert to earlier versions.<SEP>Git is a version control system that tracks changes and manages versioning of code and files in a project.<SEP>Git is a version control system that tracks changes to files and allows users to revert to earlier versions, functioning like an autosave or history system.<SEP>Git is a version control system that tracks changes to files, allowing users to revert to earlier versions.<SEP>Git is a version control system that tracks changes to code, allowing users to revert to previous states.

Repo
A repo (repository) is a project folder that holds code, files, and settings, used for organizing and versioning project content.<SEP>A repo (repository) is a project folder that holds code, files, and settings, used as the workspace unit in Claude Code.

GitHub
GitHub is an online hosting platform for repositories, functioning like a shareable cloud storage service for code.<SEP>GitHub is an online platform that hosts repositories for collaboration and sharing, functioning similarly to a public cloud storage service for code.<SEP>GitHub is an online platform where repositories are shared and collaborated on, similar to a shared Google Drive for code.<SEP>GitHub is an online platform where repositories are shared and collaborated on, similar to a shared Google Drive.<SEP>GitHub is an online platform where repositories are shared and collaborated on, referenced as a source of external links that users should verify.

VS Code
VS Code is a commonly used code editor or IDE that can be used alongside Claude.<SEP>VS Code (Visual Studio Code) is a popular code editor widely used for software development.<SEP>VS Code is a popular code editor used for software development.<SEP>VS Code is a popular code editor developed by Microsoft, inside which Claude can run.<SEP>VS Code is a popular code editor in which Claude can run; it is the basis for the anti-gravity workspace mentioned by the presenter.

Prompt Engineering
Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting clearer and more specific instructions for Claude, including assigning roles to improve output quality.<SEP>Prompt engineering is the practice of writing clearer, role-based natural-language instructions to obtain better results from AI models.<SEP>Prompt engineering is the practice of writing clearer, role-based prompts to obtain better AI results, such as instructing the AI to "act as a senior web developer."<SEP>Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting clearer, role-based, and specific prompts to achieve better results from Claude.<SEP>Prompt engineering is the practice of writing clearer, role-based instructions to obtain better results from AI models like Claude.

Cursor
Cursor is a code editor or IDE that can be used with Claude.<SEP>Cursor is a paid code editor option built on VS Code, mentioned as an alternative to Anti-Gravity.<SEP>Cursor is a paid alternative code editor used for software development.<SEP>Cursor is an alternative paid code editor, mentioned as an option alongside VS Code.<SEP>Cursor is a paid code editor alternative to VS Code, mentioned as an option for working with Claude Code.

Supabase
Supabase is a back-end platform providing server and database logic, used as a back-end tool in Claude-assisted projects.<SEP>Supabase is a back-end platform providing server, data, and logic services for web applications.<SEP>Supabase is a platform used for back-end services, serving as an example of a back-end system.<SEP>Supabase is a back-end service used as an example of a back-end platform when describing front-end/back-end architecture.

Vercel
Vercel is a front-end deployment and hosting tool used for publishing user interfaces and web apps.<SEP>Vercel is a platform used for front-end deployment, allowing users to publish web applications for others to access.<SEP>Vercel is a platform used for front-end deployment, serving as an example of a front-end hosting service.<SEP>Vercel is a front-end deployment platform used as an example of a front-end service in the context of building apps with Claude.

Notion
Notion is an application that can be integrated with Claude via the Notion API, serving as an example of an external app that Claude can interact with.<SEP>A Notion document is planned to be shared by the creator to summarize the video content and outline plans for a follow-up on Claude features.

Deployment
Deployment is the process of publishing an app or project so that others can access it.<SEP>Deployment is the process of publishing an application so that others with permission can access it.<SEP>Deployment refers to publishing a project so that others can access it.<SEP>Deployment refers to the process of publishing an application so that others can access it.

data.content:
Every Claude Code Concept Explained For Non-Techies
A 20-minute educational video explaining 23 Claude Code concepts for beginners, organized into four parts covering workspace basics, building with AI, connecting systems, and power features, plus bonus tips.<SEP>A video (20:15) created by a presenter that explains Claude and Claude Code concepts in four parts plus a bonus section, targeting non-technical audiences.

Compact Conversation
Compact conversation is a command that shrinks the current chat history to free up context window space, useful when conversation history is large.<SEP>Compact conversation is a technique to compress chat history in order to free up context window space so Claude focuses on essential information.<SEP>Compact conversation is a command that shrinks or condenses chat history so Claude uses less of the context window.<SEP>Compact conversation is a Claude Code feature that condenses chat history to save context tokens during a session.<SEP>A command in Claude Code that shrinks chat history to save context space and reduce token usage.

/Clear
/clear is a command that clears the chat context entirely to allow a fresh start.<SEP>A command in Claude Code that clears the chat context.

/Init
A command in Claude Code used to create a claude.md file for long-term project memory.

Prompt
A prompt is the natural language instruction given to Claude to direct its actions or outputs.<SEP>A prompt is a natural-language instruction given to an AI to direct its actions or outputs; clarity and specificity improve results.<SEP>A prompt is the instruction given to Claude in natural language to direct its actions.<SEP>A prompt is a natural-language instruction given to an AI model, specifying what the user wants it to do.<SEP>A prompt is a user instruction written in plain language given to Claude, analogous to ordering at a restaurant, used to direct Claude's responses and actions.

Safety Practices
Safety practices in Claude Code include verifying external GitHub links, restricting Claude access to sensitive folders, and reviewing edits when necessary.

Front End
Front end refers to the user-facing part of a web application, representing what users see and interact with directly.<SEP>Front end refers to the part of a system that users see and interact with directly.<SEP>Front end refers to the user interface layer of an application, contrasted with back-end server and data logic.<SEP>Front end refers to the part of an application that users see and interact with directly.<SEP>The front end refers to the part of an application that users see and interact with, exemplified by platforms like Vercel.

Tools
Tools in Claude Code refer to capabilities such as reading files, writing files, and running bash/shell commands, which Claude can perform if granted permission.

MCP (Model Context Protocol)
MCP is described as a "master key" that allows Claude deeper and broader access to apps, enabling it to act on the user's behalf inside applications.<SEP>MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a protocol described as a powerful "master key" that allows AI models to act across an application on a user's behalf, enabling edits and changes.<SEP>MCP is described as a "master key" that gives Claude broader in-app control, enabling it to act on a user's behalf inside an application.<SEP>MCP is described as a "master key" that provides broader access, allowing Claude to act on a user's behalf inside an application.

Slashinit (/Init)
Slashinit (/init) is a command used to create a claude.md long-term memory file at the start of a project.

Back End
Back end refers to the server, data, and logic layer of a web application, operating behind the scenes.<SEP>Back end refers to the underlying internal logic and data systems of an application.<SEP>Back end refers to the server and data logic layer of an application, contrasted with the front-end user interface.<SEP>Back end refers to the underlying functionality and data processing of an application, not visible to users.<SEP>The back end refers to the part of an application that runs behind the scenes, exemplified by platforms like Supabase.

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
RAG is a method where Claude answers queries by retrieving and using data from user-provided documents or databases for more accurate responses.<SEP>RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a method where Claude uses provided data from documents or databases to answer questions, improving accuracy.<SEP>RAG is a method where Claude retrieves information from user-supplied data to accurately answer questions, generating responses grounded in that content.

/Resume
/resume is a command that restores a recent conversation after clearing, avoiding the need to retype previous context.<SEP>A command in Claude Code that resumes a cleared or previous conversation.

Anti-Gravity
Anti-Gravity is a VS Code-based workspace used as an alternative code editor, preferred by the video creator for being free.<SEP>Anti-gravity is a code editor or IDE that integrates Claude agents, usable alongside Claude for building projects.

Ask Before Edits
Ask before edits is a permissions mode in which Claude requests confirmation before making any file edits, providing an intermediate level of safety between plan mode and bypass permission.

Token
Tokens are the unit of usage for Claude, roughly corresponding to words, used to measure input and output and determine costs.<SEP>Tokens are the units of computation and cost used by Claude, roughly corresponding to words, with Claude supporting up to 1 million tokens of input/output context.

Repository
A repository (repo) is a project folder that holds code, files, settings, and instructions for a software project.

Checkpoints & Undo
Checkpoints and Undo is a Claude Code feature that auto-saves project states and allows users to revert changes if needed.<SEP>Checkpoints & Undo is a feature where Claude auto-saves progress and provides options to revert changes to earlier states.

Claude Code 2.0
Claude Code 2.0 is a forthcoming advanced version of Claude Code, which the video creator promises to cover in a follow-up video.<SEP>Claude Code 2.0 is a newer version of Claude Code that the speaker promises to cover in a follow-up, featuring new capabilities.<SEP>Claude Code 2.0 is a forthcoming version of Claude Code teased by the presenter as the subject of a follow-up video covering more advanced features.

Notion Doc
A Notion document provided by the video creator in the video description, summarizing the 23 Claude Code concepts explained in the video.<SEP>A Notion doc is a printable/reader version of the video content that the presenter plans to share with viewers.

Tools (Read/Write/Bash)
Tools refer to capabilities granted to Claude to view files (read), create or edit files (write), and run shell commands (bash) on a user's machine, with permissions governing access.<SEP>Tools in Claude Code refer to capabilities granted to Claude, including reading files, creating/editing files (write), and running shell commands (bash), which can be controlled for safety.

Pro/Max Subscription
Pro/Max are Claude subscription plans recommended for heavy users to manage token costs more efficiently compared to pay-per-token pricing.

RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)
RAG is a method where Claude looks up and uses data fed to it to answer queries, improving accuracy.

/Init Command
The /init command initializes a project and creates the project MD file (claude.md) for long-term memory storage.<SEP>The /init command is a Claude Code command used to create a claude.md file that stores long-term project memory for a project.

/Resume Command
The /resume command is a Claude Code command used to bring back a previous conversation after the chat has been cleared.

/Clear Command
/clear is a command used to clear the session chat and reset Claude's short-term memory.<SEP>The /clear command is a Claude Code command used to clear the chat history and free up context tokens.

Repo (Repository)
A repository is a project folder that holds code, files, and settings.

Bypass Permission Mode
Bypass permission mode is a Claude Code setting that skips permission checks for convenience but carries higher risk; recommended only when the user is confident in the actions being taken.

/clear
/clear is a command that clears the current chat and context in Claude.

Pro/Max Plan
Pro/Max are paid subscription plans for Claude, recommended for users who use Claude heavily rather than paying per token.<SEP>Pro/Max are paid subscription plans for Claude recommended for heavy users to avoid high per-token costs.

Microsoft
Microsoft is the company that developed VS Code, a popular code editor.

/init
/init is a command used to initialize a project and create the claude.md long-term memory file.

-resume
-resume is a command that resumes a cleared or past conversation, avoiding the need to retype previous context.

Ask-Before-Edits
Ask-before-edits is a permission mode in Claude that prompts the user for confirmation before making any edits, recommended for live projects.

Permissions/Modes
Permissions/Modes are operational settings for Claude including plan mode, ask-before-edits, and bypass-permissions, with plan mode recommended as safest for live projects.

Bypass Permissions
Bypass permissions is a permission mode that allows Claude to act without asking for confirmation each time, convenient but risky for sensitive projects.

Claude.md (MD File)
Claude.md is a long-term memory file created for a project using the /init command, used to persist project context across sessions.

Resume Command
The resume command restores or continues a previous conversation after the session has been cleared.

Bypass-Permission Mode
Bypass-permission mode allows Claude to operate without requesting permission for each action; convenient but riskier, recommended only when the agent is trusted or mistakes can be undone.

Sub-agents
Sub-agents are specialized AI helpers that collaborate as an "AI agency," with smaller agents handling different tasks.

Notion API
The Notion API is an interface that allows external services to communicate with Notion, used as an example of an API integration.

Repository (Repo)
A repository is a project folder that holds code, files, and settings, often managed with version control.

Antigravity
Antigravity is a free code editor based on VS Code, described as the presenter's preferred option.

Terminal/CLI
The Terminal/CLI is a text-based interface used to control a computer by typing commands instead of using a graphical interface.

Ask-Before-Edits Mode
Ask-before-edits is a permissions mode in Claude that prompts the user for approval before making any edits, recommended for use on live or sensitive projects.
